question.text: An Indian company receives an export payment of EUR 500,000 in one month. To hedge the currency risk, it enters a forward contract to sell EUR. If the forward EUR/INR rate is 84.00, what INR amount is the company guaranteed to receive?

answer.text: The amount depends on the spot rate at maturity

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 29, in an exporter-forward structure the rate is fixed on the trade date and EUR is delivered for INR at maturity. EUR 500,000 x 84.00 = INR 4,20,00,000, i.e. INR 4.2 crore. The Trap: The actual spot rate at maturity is irrelevant; the whole point of the forward is to lock in the contracted rate. Note: Page 38 reinforces that a forward contract is a future-date transaction at a predetermined price, giving the exporter certainty over INR cash flow.
